transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-18
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (Redwood Solutions), Maya Lopez (Silverpine CTO), Jon Park (Infra Eng), Priya Singh (ML Eng), Samir Desai (Security)

Summary: quick discovery to nail down whether Silverpine needs Dedicated reserved GPUs behind VPC, isolation requirements, burst / warm-pool strategy and compliance gating. Talked through usage patterns, fallback to hosted, encryption/KMS and pilot plan.

Topics: reserved capacity sizing, tenant isolation, warm pool/prewarm, cost/latency tradeoffs, SOC2/KMS/HSM, rollout timeline, benchmark plan

Transcript:
00:00 Avery Chen: hey everybody, thanks for joining, um we'll run about 45 minutes, we're here to understand your workload and see if Dedicated or Private makes sense versus Hosted. quick intros?
00:12 Maya Lopez: hi I'm Maya, CTO at Silverpine, we build real-time analytics for financial ops, high qps on short prompts, sometimes long sequences for reports.
00:22 Jon Park: Jon, infra, we care about isolation and predictable tail latency, multi-tenant customers, need to avoid noisy neighbor.
00:27 Priya Singh: Priya, ML, we'll be running several model families, Llama-2 variants and a few quantized weights, and some larger encoder-decoder models for summarization.
00:36 Diego Ramos: cool, thanks. quick question on traffic shape — peak qps, burst duration, and percent of long sequences?
00:44 Priya Singh: baseline qps 120 qps, peaks to ~1.8k for 3-5 minutes during end-of-day, maybe twice a day. long sequences ~8% of tokens, most are sub 256 tokens.
00:56 Avery Chen: ok that burst pattern's helpful. are you planning to do a single reserved pool or per-tenant dedicated pools?
01:05 Maya Lopez: for now we want logical isolation for high-value customers, but not full hardware per-tenant. so soft tenant fencing with cgroups maybe, but we need strict data separation for some regulated clients.
01:17 Diego Ramos: Redwood Dedicated supports node-level isolation (reserved pools) plus tenant sharding; we can do reserved node sets with pre-allocated GPUs and also VLAN/VPC peering for network isolation. default approach is shared reserved pool with strong scheduler tenancy — does that map to what you want?
01:33 Jon Park: yes but can you guarantee noisy neighbor doesn't cause tail latency spikes? our SLO is p95 < 200ms for short prompts, and p99 needs to be consistent for SLAs.
01:45 Diego Ramos: right. two levers: warm pool and prewarming KV cache for hot models, and strict CPU/GPU accounting to avoid eviction. for p99— we recommend dedicated warm pools for top customers and automatic fallback to smaller model variants if saturation occurs.
01:58 Maya Lopez: fallback to smaller model variants? can you explain the rollback path if reserved pool saturates?
02:04 Diego Ramos: sure — policy routing. typical policy: route to Dedicated reserved nodes first; if queue depth crosses threshold, fallback to a compatible hosted variant or quantized model in the same region. we keep consistency by pinning model versions and using cached KV to reduce cold-starts. there is a small config to control degradation preference — cost vs latency.
02:28 Priya Singh: hmm ok. Our compliance team will ask about keys and telemetry. Samir, can you add?
02:33 Samir Desai: yes two main things — KMS/HSM integration for customer-managed keys, and audit logs retained 12 months with immutable trails. can you support HSM-backed KMS in dedicated/private?
02:43 Diego Ramos: yes, Private or Dedicated with VPC supports KMS integrations, we can integrate with customer KMS or support HSM via partners. audit logs and per-token provenance are available but retention and export need to be configured.
02:55 Maya Lopez: also data residency — some customers require EU-only. can you run Dedicated in specific regions?
03:02 Avery Chen: we have regional Dedicated capacity, yes. you can pin to region and we support routing by region with fallback.
03:10 Jon Park: what about encryption at rest on the node and ephemeral caches?
03:15 Diego Ramos: everything at-rest is encrypted by default; KV caches are encrypted and tied to the node and key material. for extra assurance we can enable disk-level encryption with customer keys. small caveat: some quantized formats write intermediate artifacts — we can lock those down in Private deployments.
03:34 Priya Singh: Performance: do you have benchmarks for the models we run? want real-world numbers for p95/p99 and token cost.
03:42 Diego Ramos: yes, we have perf profiles and we'll run a custom benchmark with your payloads. propose a 2-week pilot: 1) bench on equivalent GPU (NVIDIA H100-like), 2) run warm-pool prewarm tests mimicking end-of-day bursts, 3) evaluate cost/latency and failover behavior. I can send a test script.
03:58 Maya Lopez: sounds good. how long to provision reserved pool?
04:02 Avery Chen: typical lead time depends on region and commit; for Dedicated reserved pools we can provision prewarmed nodes in 3-10 business days if capacity available, longer if special SKUs. Private/on-prem has a different onboarding window.
04:15 Jon Park: we may need to evaluate a hybrid — some tenants on Dedicated, others on Hosted for cost. do you support mixing pooling strategies?
04:23 Diego Ramos: yes, smart routing can split by tenant, route premium traffic to reserved pool, default to Hosted otherwise. also autoscaling policies can burst into a 'hotpool' or fallback to Hosted model variant.
04:36 Priya Singh: about prewarming — what's the KV cache warm strategy? do you prepopulate from sample prompts?
04:42 Diego Ramos: two approaches: prefix caching using recent requests, or explicit prewarm scripts where you feed representative prompts to populate KV. for your 3-5 minute bursts we'd recommend persistent warm workers plus a short prewarm window triggered on forecasted events.
05:00 Maya Lopez: what's our expected cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated for our profile?
05:04 Avery Chen: roughly Hosted is higher per-token but no commit; Dedicated reduces per-token cost by 30-60% depending on utilization. big driver is utilization during peak windows — if you have predictable peaks and commit, Dedicated is more economical. we'll share an estimate with your numbers.
05:20 Samir Desai: security question — if we use Dedicated in VPC, how's access control to the control plane and logs?
05:26 Diego Ramos: control plane access is via customer SSO (SAML/SCIM), RBAC roles, and you can restrict console access. logs are streamed to customer SIEM over secure transport; we also support private control plane options for Private deployments.
05:40 Priya Singh: any gotchas around quantization or kernel selection for our model family? we've seen hallucination increase with aggressive quantization.
05:47 Diego Ramos: yes, quantization can change output characteristics; Redwood Optimize will profile models and recommend quant settings per workload. for critical outputs we recommend lighter quant or mixed precision and more evals. we'll include eval thresholds in the pilot so we can catch quality regressions.
06:05 Maya Lopez: timeline-wise we want a pilot in mid-June and a potential Q3 production rollout. SLA wise, what uptime/latency guarantees for Dedicated?
06:14 Avery Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA for uptime—99.9% or negotiable on enterprise tier, and latency SLOs depend on config. we'll map your p95/p99 requirements and document SLOs in the contract.
06:26 Jon Park: if the reserved pool is saturated and hosted fallback kicks in, how do you notify and can we throttle?
06:32 Diego Ramos: yes, notifications through Console/Slack and webhooks. you can set throttles per route and automatic reject or degrade policies. also conservative burst policies can be set to prefer cost or prefer latency.
06:46 Priya Singh: ok one more: telemetry — can we send token-level traces to our tracing system?
06:52 Diego Ramos: yes, token-level traces can be exported with sampling; full token export option is available behind higher retention plans. note PII handling must be configured.
07:03 Avery Chen: recap — Redwood to send SOC2 + deployment diagrams, benchmark plan & scripts, pricing options for reserved term (6/12/24 mo), and we'll schedule a 2-week pilot kickoff mid-June. Silverpine to send traffic CSV and compliance questions.
07:18 Maya Lopez: thanks. we'll review and come back with any blockers.
